newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan drafts rules for post-1997 Hong Kong trade.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan drafts rules for post-1997 Hong Kong trade.

text.p: A Taiwan agency on Thursday completed draft regulations for economic ties with Hong Kong following its return to China in July after 150 years of British rule.

Officials said the rules treat most Hong Kong business like any other foreign investment, but restrict some large or sensitive deals that might be damaging to Taiwan -- much the way the island now screens investments in China itself.

The rules require investors to seek approval for important or large-scale projects or face heavy fines and punishment, said Chintan Huang, deputy executive secretary of the state Investment Commission.
Officials have yet to determine what levels of investment will require government screening, Huang said by telephone.
"The draft, approved in a cross-department meeting, will lay the legal framework for our continued trade and investment with Hong Kong after July 1, 1997," Huang said.
The draft will be sent to the cabinet before the end of April for final approval before China resumes control of Hong Kong at midnight on June 30.
The measures also would apply to investment and trade in Macau after its scheduled return to Chinese sovereignty from Portugal on December 20, 1999, Huang said.
Investment officials said that in principle, investments of up to US$5 million by individuals and US$20 million by institutions would need no prior approval from the commission.
Prior approval would be needed for investments in certain businesses, including financial, insurance and travel agency services, officials said.
Taiwan's parliament approved on March 18 the long-expected Hong Kong-Macau Relations Act to allow continued relations with the two territories after they revert to Chinese rule.

Under the law, the two territories will be treated as Special Administration Zones to avoid Taiwan's ban on direct contact with China that has been imposed since the two sides split after the end of a civil war in 1949.

Some 30,000 Taiwan companies are estimated to have channeled as much as US$30 billion to the mainland through Hong Kong and elsewhere since Taiwan eased the ban in the late 1980s, allowing indirect economic relations.
Taiwan's 1996 exports to Hong kong stood at US$26.8 billion -- most destined for transshipment ot China -- while imports totalled just US$1.7 billion.
